title: Abetment of a thing
old_text: A person abets the doing of a thing, who instigates any person to do that thing; or engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing; or intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.
new_text: A person abets the doing of a thing, who instigates any person to do that thing; or engages with one or more other person or persons in any conspiracy for the doing of that thing; or intentionally aids, by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing.
punishment_old: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed according to consequential provisions (IPC ss. 109-120).
punishment_new: Substantive definition; punishment prescribed according to consequential provisions (BNS ss. 49-60).
explanation: Defines the three foundational modes of abetment: instigation, conspiracy coupled with an overt act or illegal omission, and intentional aiding. The operative legal principles and explanations remain identical to IPC Section 107.

title: Abettor
old_text: A person abets an offence, who abets either the commission of an offence, or the commission of an act which would be an offence, if committed by a person capable by law of committing an offence with the same intention or knowledge.
new_text: A person abets an offence, who abets either the commission of an offence, or the commission of an act which would be an offence, if committed by a person capable by law of committing an offence with the same intention or knowledge.
punishment_old: Definition of abettor; punishment follows consequential sections.
punishment_new: Definition of abettor; punishment follows consequential sections.
explanation: Defines an abettor and clarifies that abetting an illegal omission is punishable, and the person abetted need not possess legal capacity (e.g. child or person of unsound mind). All statutory explanations from IPC Section 108 are retained.

title: Abetment in India of offences outside India
old_text: A person abets an offence within the meaning of this Code who, in India, abets the commission of any act without and beyond India which would constitute an offence if committed in India.
new_text: A person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, in India, abets the commission of any act without and beyond India which would constitute an offence if committed in India.
punishment_old: Punished as if the offence abetted had been committed in India.
punishment_new: Punished as if the offence abetted had been committed in India.
explanation: Governs extra-territorial offences initiated from India, establishing that instigating or aiding a crime abroad from within Indian territory is punishable as if committed in India. Renumbered from IPC Section 108A.

title: Abetment outside India for offence in India
old_text: None (extra-territorial jurisdiction was broadly inferred under IPC ss. 3-4, but no dedicated section specifically penalized abetment committed outside India targeting crimes inside India).
new_text: A person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, without and beyond India, abets the commission of any act in India which would constitute an offence if committed in India.
punishment_old: Not codified as a standalone abetment section in IPC.
punishment_new: Punished as an abettor of the corresponding offence committed in India.
explanation: A newly introduced provision in BNS closing a cross-border jurisdictional loophole. It explicitly penalizes foreign actors and entities outside India who instigate, conspire, or aid in crimes executed within Indian territory.

title: Punishment of abetment if the act abetted is committed in consequence and where no express provision is made for its punishment
old_text: Whoever abets any offence shall, if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Code for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.
new_text: Whoever abets any offence shall, if the act abetted is committed in consequence of the abetment, and no express provision is made by this Sanhita for the punishment of such abetment, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence.
punishment_old: Punishment provided for the principal offence abetted.
punishment_new: Punishment provided for the principal offence abetted.
explanation: The baseline sentencing rule for abetment: when the crime is successfully completed and no special punishment is provided, the abettor receives the exact punishment prescribed for the principal offence. Renumbered from IPC Section 109.

title: Punishment of abetment if person abetted does act with different intention from that of abettor
old_text: Whoever abets the commission of an offence shall, if the person abetted does the act with a different intention or knowledge from that of the abettor, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence which would have been committed if the act had been done with the intention or knowledge of the abettor.
new_text: Whoever abets the commission of an offence shall, if the person abetted does the act with a different intention or knowledge from that of the abettor, be punished with the punishment provided for the offence which would have been committed if the act had been done with the intention or knowledge of the abettor.
punishment_old: Punishment for the offence that would have been committed had the act matched the abettor's mens rea.
punishment_new: Punishment for the offence that would have been committed had the act matched the abettor's mens rea.
explanation: Judges the abettor's criminal liability based on their own mens rea, regardless of whether the actual perpetrator acted with a distinct intention or knowledge. Renumbered from IPC Section 110.

title: Liability of abettor when one act abetted and different act done
old_text: When an act is abetted and a different act is done, the abettor is liable for the act done, in the same manner and to the same extent as if he had directly abetted it, provided the act done was a probable consequence of the abetment.
new_text: When an act is abetted and a different act is done, the abettor is liable for the act done, in the same manner and to the same extent as if he had directly abetted it, provided the act done was a probable consequence of the abetment.
punishment_old: Punished for the divergent act as if directly abetted, if it was a probable consequence.
punishment_new: Punished for the divergent act as if directly abetted, if it was a probable consequence.
explanation: Codifies the doctrine of probable consequence: an abettor remains liable for a different act committed by the perpetrator only if that act was a natural and foreseeable outcome of the abetment. Renumbered from IPC Section 111.

title: Abettor when liable to cumulative punishment for act abetted and for act done
old_text: If the act for which the abettor is liable under the last preceding section is committed in addition to the act abetted, and constitutes a distinct offence, the abettor is liable to punishment for each of the offences.
new_text: If the act for which the abettor is liable under section 51 is committed in addition to the act abetted, and constitutes a distinct offence, the abettor is liable to punishment for each of the offences.
punishment_old: Cumulative punishment for both the act abetted and the distinct collateral offence committed.
punishment_new: Cumulative punishment for both the act abetted and the distinct collateral offence committed.
explanation: Permits cumulative sentencing where both the originally abetted crime and an additional distinct probable consequential crime are carried out. Renumbered from IPC Section 112.

title: Liability of abettor for an effect caused by the act abetted different from that intended by the abettor
old_text: When an act is abetted with the intention of causing a particular effect, and causes a different effect, the abettor is liable for the effect caused, in the same manner as if he had abetted the act with that intention, provided he knew that the act abetted was likely to cause that effect.
new_text: When an act is abetted with the intention of causing a particular effect, and causes a different effect, the abettor is liable for the effect caused, in the same manner as if he had abetted the act with that intention, provided he knew that the act abetted was likely to cause that effect.
punishment_old: Punished for the resulting effect as if intended, provided knowledge of likelihood is proven.
punishment_new: Punished for the resulting effect as if intended, provided knowledge of likelihood is proven.
explanation: Addresses aggravated outcomes (such as grievous hurt escalating to death). The abettor is held responsible for the escalated effect if they knew it was likely to occur. Renumbered from IPC Section 113.

title: Abettor present when offence is committed
old_text: Whenever any person, who if absent would be liable to be punished as an abettor, is present when the act or offence for which he would be punishable in consequence of the abetment is committed, he shall be deemed to have committed such act or offence.
new_text: Whenever any person, who if absent would be liable to be punished as an abettor, is present when the act or offence for which he would be punishable in consequence of the abetment is committed, he shall be deemed to have committed such act or offence.
punishment_old: Deemed to be a principal offender and punished for committing the offence directly.
punishment_new: Deemed to be a principal offender and punished for committing the offence directly.
explanation: Creates a legal fiction under which a prior abettor present at the crime scene during commission is deemed a principal offender rather than an abettor. Renumbered from IPC Section 114.

title: Abetment of offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
old_text: Whoever abets the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence of the abetment, be punished with imprisonment up to seven years and fine; and if hurt is caused, up to fourteen years and fine.
new_text: Whoever abets the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence of the abetment, be punished with imprisonment up to seven years and fine; and if hurt is caused, up to fourteen years and fine.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine; if hurt is caused, imprisonment up to 14 years and fine.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine; if hurt is caused, imprisonment up to 14 years and fine.
explanation: Penalizes uncompleted abetment of capital or life-imprisonment crimes. If physical hurt occurs as a consequence, the maximum sentence doubles to 14 years. Renumbered from IPC Section 115.

title: Abetment of offence punishable with imprisonment
old_text: Whoever abets an offence punishable with imprisonment shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term provided for that offence, or with fine, or both.
new_text: Whoever abets an offence punishable with imprisonment shall, if that offence be not committed in consequence, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term provided for that offence, or with fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1/4 of longest term, or fine, or both; if abettor or person abetted is a public servant bound to prevent, up to 1/2 of longest term, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 1/4 of longest term, or fine, or both; if abettor or person abetted is a public servant bound to prevent, up to 1/2 of longest term, or fine, or both.
explanation: Establishes proportional sentencing (one-fourth of the statutory term) for abetting imprisonable offences that do not take place. The penalty is increased to one-half if a public servant responsible for crime prevention is involved. Renumbered from IPC Section 116.

title: Abetting commission of offence by the public or by more than ten persons
old_text: Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
new_text: Whoever abets the commission of an offence by the public generally or by any number or class of persons exceeding ten, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or with fine, or with both.
explanation: Penalizes mass incitement, public instigation, or distributing criminal calls to action targeted at the general public or crowds exceeding ten individuals. Renumbered from IPC Section 117.

title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
old_text: Whoever intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, voluntarily conceals, by any act or omission, the existence of a design to commit such offence, shall be punished.
new_text: Whoever intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life, voluntarily conceals, by any act or omission, the existence of a design to commit such offence, shall be punished.
punishment_old: If offence committed: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine; if not committed: imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
punishment_new: If offence committed: imprisonment up to 7 years and fine; if not committed: imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
explanation: Criminalizes intentional concealment of plots to carry out crimes punishable by death or life imprisonment. Renumbered from IPC Section 118.

title: A public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent
old_text: Whoever, being a public servant, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence which it is his duty as such public servant to prevent, voluntarily conceals the design to commit such offence, shall be punished.
new_text: Whoever, being a public servant, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence which it is his duty as such public servant to prevent, voluntarily conceals the design to commit such offence, shall be punished.
punishment_old: If committed: up to half the longest term or fine or both; if capital/life: up to 10 years and fine; if not committed: up to one-fourth term or fine or both.
punishment_new: If committed: up to half the longest term or fine or both; if capital/life: up to 10 years and fine; if not committed: up to one-fourth term or fine or both.
explanation: Penalizes public servants who conceal criminal plans they are legally duty-bound to suppress. Renumbered from IPC Section 119.

title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
old_text: Whoever, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with imprisonment, voluntarily conceals the existence of a design to commit such offence, shall be punished.
new_text: Whoever, intending to facilitate or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby facilitate the commission of an offence punishable with imprisonment, voluntarily conceals the existence of a design to commit such offence, shall be punished.
punishment_old: If offence committed: imprisonment up to 1/4 of longest term, or fine, or both; if not committed: imprisonment up to 1/8 of longest term, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: If offence committed: imprisonment up to 1/4 of longest term, or fine, or both; if not committed: imprisonment up to 1/8 of longest term, or fine, or both.
explanation: Penalizes concealment of designs to commit general imprisonable offences, with graduated liability based on whether the offence was actually carried out. Renumbered from IPC Section 120.

title: Criminal conspiracy
old_text: IPC Section 120A defined criminal conspiracy as an agreement between two or more persons to do an illegal act or an act by illegal means; IPC Section 120B provided separate punishments based on offence severity.
new_text: Sub-section (1) defines criminal conspiracy (agreement to do an illegal act, or legal act by illegal means, with an overt act required for minor offences); sub-section (2) prescribes punishments matching principal abetment or imprisonment up to 6 months/fine for other cases.
punishment_old: IPC 120B(1): Punished as abettor if offence punishable with death/life/rigorous imprisonment >= 2 yrs; IPC 120B(2): Imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: BNS 61(2): Punished as abettor if offence punishable with death, life, or rigorous imprisonment >= 2 years; in other conspiracies, imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both.
explanation: Merges the substantive definition (IPC 120A) and punishment provisions (IPC 120B) into a single unified section. The requirement of an agreement and the exception dispensing with overt acts for serious felonies remain unchanged.

title: Punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment
old_text: Whoever attempts to commit an offence punishable by this Code with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, and in such attempt does any act towards the commission of the offence, where no express provision is made, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one-half of the longest term, or fine, or both.
new_text: Whoever attempts to commit an offence punishable by this Sanhita with imprisonment for life or imprisonment, and in such attempt does any act towards the commission of the offence, where no express provision is made, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one-half of the longest term, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to one-half of the longest term provided for that offence, or fine, or both.
punishment_new: Imprisonment up to one-half of the longest term provided for that offence, or fine, or both.
explanation: Relocates the general attempt provision from the final section of the IPC (Section 511) directly into Chapter IV alongside Abetment and Criminal Conspiracy, grouping all inchoate crimes together logically. The sentencing metric remains up to one-half the maximum term.
